newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline ends slightly up as bulls bank on arb.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline ends slightly up as bulls bank on arb.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices ended slightly higher on Wednesday in quiet activity with bullish traders betting that an open arbitrage to the United States and rising seasonal demand will lift the market.
But no cargo deals were heard done and the Queen's Day holiday in the Netherlands and several other European holidays into Monday put a cap on the amount of deals done.
Eurograde barges ended up $2 at $198 fob ARA, where two 2,000 tonne trades were done this morning. Regular unleaded was notionally valued at about $191/$192.
"On the cargo side it's very strong and there is not much availability to put pressure on the (barge) market," one trader said.
Cargoes were valued at $201/$205 cif and at $193/$197 fob.
A trader at a major said he was also bullish prices because of the open arbitrage, seasonal factors and expectations for U.S. demand to kick in.
Other traders said some cat gas had also been shipped out of the Med in the second-half of April for the U.S.
May NYMEX gasoline futures, which shot up a cent a gallon on Tuesday, were about 0.50 cent higher ahead of its expiry at the close today.

Wednesday's Energy Infromation Administration data showed a 100,000 barrel build in U.S. gasoline inventories last week, against a decline of 408,000 barrels reported last night by the American Petroleum Institute.
